Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verses 6–8:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾ (45:6)

He, the Exalted, says: These verses and proofs, O Muhammad, from your Lord, over His creation, We recite to you in truth. That is: We inform you about them in truth, not in falsehood, as the polytheists of your people inform about their gods falsely, that they bring them near to Allah in closeness. ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will you believe?﴾ He, the Exalted, says to the polytheists who associate others with Him: Then in what statement, O people, after this statement of Allah, which He recites to you, and after His proof against you and His evidences by which He has guided you to His oneness, that there is no lord for you besides Him, will you believe, if you have denied His statement and His verses? This interpretation accords with the reading of those who recite ﴿tu'minūna﴾ (you believe) in the second person, as an address from Allah to the polytheists with these words, and this is the reading of the general body of the Kufan reciters.

As for the reading of those who recite ﴿yu'minūna﴾ (they believe) with the letter yā', its meaning is: Then in what statement, O Muhammad, after the statement of Allah which He recites to you and these His verses with which He admonished these polytheists and reminded them, will these polytheists believe? This is the reading of the general body of the reciters of Medina and Basra. Both readings have a correct aspect and a comprehensible interpretation, and whichever of the two readings the reciter recites is correct in our view. However, I incline toward reading it with the yā', since it occurs in a context of verses that preceded it in the form of a statement, namely His words: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾ and ﴿for a people who reason﴾.

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth. Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾ (45:6)

He, the Exalted, says: These verses and proofs, O Muhammad, from your Lord, over His creation, We recite to you in truth. That is: We inform you about them in truth, not in falsehood, as the polytheists of your people inform about their gods falsely, that they bring them near to Allah in closeness. ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His verses will you believe?﴾ He, the Exalted, says to the polytheists who associate others with Him: Then in what statement, O people, after this statement of Allah, which He recites to you, and after His proof against you and His evidences by which He has guided you to His oneness, that there is no lord for you besides Him, will you believe, if you have denied His statement and His verses? This interpretation accords with the reading of those who recite ﴿tu'minūna﴾ (you believe) in the second person, as an address from Allah to the polytheists with these words, and this is the reading of the general body of the Kufan reciters.

As for the reading of those who recite ﴿yu'minūna﴾ (they believe) with the letter yā', its meaning is: Then in what statement, O Muhammad, after the statement of Allah which He recites to you and these His verses with which He admonished these polytheists and reminded them, will these polytheists believe? This is the reading of the general body of the reciters of Medina and Basra. Both readings have a correct aspect and a comprehensible interpretation, and whichever of the two readings the reciter recites is correct in our view. However, I incline toward reading it with the yā', since it occurs in a context of verses that preceded it in the form of a statement, namely His words: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾ and ﴿for a people who reason﴾.

**Mention of those who said this:**

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 14:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God, so that He may recompense a people for what they have been earning﴾ (45:14).

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to those who affirm God and follow you: let them forgive those who do not fear the might (ba's) of God, His encounters (waqa'i'ihi) and His vengeance (naqmihi), when those people inflict harm and injury upon them. ﴿So that He may recompense a people for what they have been earning﴾ means: God will recompense those polytheists who harm them in the Hereafter, so that His punishment will befall them for the sins they earned in the world, and then for their harming the people of faith in God.

Those who have interpreted it have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God, so that He may recompense a people for what they have been earning﴾. He said: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to turn away from the polytheists when they harmed him, and they used to mock him and deny him. So God, mighty and majestic, commanded him to fight the polytheists entirely. Therefore this verse is among the abrogated (mansukh).

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God ﴿those who do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: They do not care about the blessings (ni'am) of God or His vengeance (niqam).

Al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: They do not care about the blessings of God. This verse is abrogated by God's command to fight the polytheists. We only say that it is abrogated because the consensus (ijma') of the interpreters holds that this is so.

Those who said that:

We have already mentioned the report on this from Ibn Abbas. Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: It was abrogated by what is in al-Anfal: ﴿So if you overcome them in war, then scatter those behind them, that perhaps they will remember﴾ [8:57], and in Bara'a: ﴿Fight the polytheists entirely as they fight you entirely﴾ [9:36]. He commanded fighting them until they bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: It was abrogated by ﴿then kill the polytheists﴾ [9:5].

It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: This is abrogated; God commanded fighting them in Surat Bara'a.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, he said: Anbasa related to us, from one whom he mentioned, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: It was abrogated by what is in al-Hajj: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought, because they have been wronged﴾ [22:39].

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of God﴾. He said: These are the polytheists. He said: This has been abrogated, and their fighting and severity against them was made obligatory.

The jussive form of ﴿yaghfiru﴾ (let them forgive) is the jussive (majzum) by analogy with the conditional and the condition, though it is not actually conditional; rather, it is because it is apparent in speech in the pattern of such, so it is given the same i'rab as it. This has been explained before.

The readers (qurra') differed regarding the reading of His words ﴿li-yajziya qawman﴾ (so that He may recompense a people). Some of the readers of Medina, Basra and Kufa read ﴿li-yajziya﴾ with the letter ya', as a report from God that He recompenses and rewards them. And some of the common readers of Kufa read ﴿li-najziya﴾ with the letter nun, as a report from God about Himself. It is reported from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he used to read ﴿li-yujza qawman﴾ in the passive form (ma lam yusamma fa'iluhu), and this, according to the way of Arabic speech, is a grammatical error (lahn). [[The speech of the Arabs is not a proof for the reading, but the reading is a proof for their speech.]] Unless he meant: "so that the recompense may recompense a people," with the recompense (al-jaza') being understood and made nominative, so that ﴿li-yujzi﴾ becomes a valid aspect of the reading, though it is far-fetched. [[It is permissible that the agent be the substitute for the agent, which is His words ﴿for what they have been earning﴾.]]

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that reading it with the ya' and with the nun, as mentioned from the readings of the regional centres (al-amsar), is permissible with whichever of these two readings the reader recites. As for reading it as you mentioned from Abu Ja'far, it is, in my view, not permissible, for two reasons. The first: it contradicts what the readers have upheld as proof, and I hold it impermissible to oppose what has come down widely (mustafidan) among them. The second: it is further from correctness in Arabic, except by forcing the speech away from its well-known manner.

[[His words: "it is not permissible" — this is an error, because the reading is a sound, transmitted (mutawatir) reading of the ten, equal in authority to the seven.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ (45:15)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: whoever of God's servants does righteous deeds by obeying Him, complying with His command and refraining from what He forbids, the benefit of that righteous deed accrues to his own soul, and by it he seeks to free his soul from the punishment of God. He obeys his Lord for no other reason, since nothing else benefits him, and God is free of need from the deeds of every doer. ﴿And whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ means: whoever spoils his deeds in this world by disobeying his Lord in them, and by opposing His command and prohibition in them, then the harm falls upon his own soul, because he has destroyed it thereby and brought upon it the wrath of God, and he has harmed no one but himself. ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ means: then you, O people, all of you, will return to your Lord after your deaths, and the good-doer among you will be recompensed for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. So whoever of you comes before Him with a righteous deed will be rewarded with a righteous reward, and whoever of you comes before Him with an evil deed will be rewarded with an evil recompense.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 45, verses 16–17:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture and authority and prophethood, and We provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds﴾ [45:16].

His saying, the Exalted, "And We had certainly given..." — O Muhammad — "...the Children of Israel the Scripture," meaning the Torah and the Gospel. "And authority," meaning understanding of the Scripture and knowledge of the sunnahs (ways) that were not revealed in the Scripture. "And prophethood," meaning: We made among them prophets and messengers to the creation. "And We provided for them of the good things," meaning: We fed them from the good things of Our provisions, and that is what He fed them of manna and quail. "And We preferred them over the worlds," meaning: We preferred them over the worlds of the people of their time, in the days and the reign of Pharaoh, in their region, in Egypt and al-Sham.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter. And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of animosity among themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾ [45:17].

His saying, the Exalted: We gave the Children of Israel clear matters of Our command, by sending down to them the Torah, in which is the detailing of every thing. "And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of animosity among themselves," seeking leadership, and abandoning, on their part, the clarification of Allah, blessed and exalted, in His revelation.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾.

His saying, the Exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, will judge between the disputing Children of Israel out of animosity among themselves on the Day of Resurrection, concerning what they used to differ about in the world, after the knowledge that He had given them and the clarification that came to them from it, and then the one who is in the right will prevail over the one who is in falsehood by the decisive judgment between them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 18–19:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the matter, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know. Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the Ally of the righteous.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Then We placed you, O Muhammad, after what We gave the Children of Israel, whose description I have given you, ﴿on a path of the matter﴾, meaning: on a way, a sunnah and a method of Our command, which We commanded those messengers before you. ﴿So follow it﴾, meaning: follow that shari'ah (sacred law, path) which We have placed for you. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾, meaning: do not follow what those ignorant of Allah, who do not recognize the truth from falsehood, call you to, lest you act upon it and perish if you act upon it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter, so follow it﴾, he said: He means: on guidance from the matter and clear proof.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter, so follow it﴾: The shari'ah is the obligations, the limits, the commands and the prohibitions, so follow it. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying (Then We placed you on a path of the matter): He said: The shari'ah is the religion. And he recited ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you﴾, and said: Noah is the first of them and you are the last of them.

And regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all﴾:

And His saying: ﴿and guidance﴾

* *

And His saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Or do those who committed evil deeds in the world, and denied the messengers of Allah, and opposed the command of their Lord, and worshipped other than Him, think that We will make them in the Hereafter like those who believed in Allah and affirmed His messengers and did righteous deeds, obeying Allah and sincerely devoting worship to Him alone, apart from the rivals and deities besides Him? As:

* *

And His saying: ﴿[that] their living and their dying will be alike﴾

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿alike (sawa')﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some readers of Kufa, recited it ﴿sawaʾun﴾ with a nominative ending, holding that the statement ends at His saying ﴿those who believe﴾, and they made the predicate of His saying ﴿that We will make them﴾, the words ﴿like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. Then they began a new statement about the equality of the state of the believer's living and dying, and the disbeliever's living and dying, and they put ﴿sawaʾun﴾ in the nominative as a subject with this meaning. A group of the interpreters followed this meaning in their explanation of it.

Mention of who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿alike is their living and their dying﴾, he said: "The believer in this world and the Hereafter is a believer, and the disbeliever in this world and the Hereafter is a disbeliever."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Shaybans, from Layth, regarding His saying ﴿alike is their living and their dying﴾, he said: "The believer is raised as a believer, living and dead, and the disbeliever is raised as a disbeliever, living and dead."

The statement, when recited with a nominative ending, may bear another meaning than the one we have mentioned from Mujahid and Layth, namely that it is directed to: "Or do those who committed evil deeds think that We will make them and the believers equal in life and death?" meaning: they are not equal. Then ﴿alike﴾ is put in the nominative on this meaning, since it is indeclinable, as one says: "I passed by a man better than you, his father," and "your kinsman is good," where "your kinsman" and "better" are in the nominative because they are in the manner of nouns; and if a verb had occupied their place in the form of a noun, it would have been only in the accusative. Likewise His saying ﴿sawaʾun﴾. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it ﴿sawaʾan﴾ with an accusative ending, meaning: Did they think that We would make them and those who believed and did righteous deeds equal?

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations in the recitations of the regions, and each has been recited by the people of knowledge of the Qur'an, and both are sound in meaning; so whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

The grammarians differed concerning the grammatical reason for the accusative and nominative of His saying ﴿sawaʾ﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: ﴿sawaʾun maḥyāhum wa mamātuhum﴾ is in the nominative. Others said: the living and dying refer to the disbelievers entirely; He said ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, then He said "alike is the living and dying of the disbelievers," meaning: their living is an equal living, and their dying is an equal dying, so ﴿alike﴾ is in the nominative as a beginning. He said: whoever explains the living and dying as belonging to both disbelievers and believers, the accusative and nominative of ﴿alike﴾ are permissible in this meaning, because whoever makes ﴿alike﴾ mean "equal" should by analogy make it agree with what precedes it, since it is a qualifier; and whoever makes it mean "equality" should make it nominative, since it is a noun, unless he makes "their living and dying" an apposition and makes ﴿alike﴾ accusative as "equality"; and if he wishes, he may put ﴿alike﴾ in the nominative when it has the sense of "equal," as you say: "I passed by a man better than you, his father," because it is a qualifier that is not declined; and the nominative is better.

Some grammarians of Kufa said: His saying ﴿alike is their living﴾ may be with an accusative or nominative ﴿alike﴾, and "their living and their dying" is in the position of the nominative, in the manner of His saying: "I saw the people alike, their young and their old," with an accusative ﴿alike﴾, because he makes it a verb due to what has returned to the people from their mention. He said: The Arabs sometimes make ﴿alike﴾ in the manner of a noun, like "your kinsman," so they say: "I saw your people alike, their young and their old," which is like your saying: "I passed by a man whose father is sufficient for you." He said: If you put in place of ﴿alike﴾ "equal," it would not be nominative, but we make it follow what precedes it, differing from ﴿alike﴾, because "equal" is a description of the people, and because ﴿alike﴾ is like a verbal noun, and a verbal noun is a noun. He said: If you made "their living and their dying" accusative, it would be a valid reading, meaning: We would make them equal in their living and their dying.

Others among them said: The meaning is that he who committed evil deeds is not equal to the believer in life or in death, on the basis that it occupied the place of a predicate, being the predicate of "We will make." He said: The accusative is for predicates, as you say: "I made your brothers alike, their young and their old," and it is permissible to put it in the nominative, because ﴿alike﴾ is indeclinable. He said: As for one who says: ﴿Or do those who committed evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, making "like those who" the predicate, then begins with ﴿alike﴾ and puts in the nominative what follows it, and "that their living and dying" is in the accusative of ﴿alike﴾ only. The correct explanation of this matter has already been made clear by us.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 22:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (22)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾, for justice and truth, not as those ignorant of Allah supposed, that He would make the one who commits evil deeds, disobeying Him and opposing His command, equal to those who believe and do righteous deeds, in life and in death. For that would be the act of one who is not characterized by justice and fairness. Exalted is His praise: He did not create the heavens and the earth for injustice and oppression, but We created them in truth and justice. And it is part of the truth that We distinguish between the judgment of the evildoer and the doer of good, in the immediate and in the hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: that Allah may reward every doer for what he has done of the deed of creating the heavens and the earth, rewarding the good-doer with goodness and the evildoer with what he deserves, not that He should deprive the good-doer of the reward of his goodness and lay upon him the crime of another so as to punish him, or give the evildoer the reward of another's goodness so as to honor him. Rather, He does so that each may be recompensed for what his hands have earned, and they will not be wronged in the recompense of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 23:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and has put a covering upon his sight? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god﴾. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Have you seen him who has taken his religion according to his desire, so that he does not desire anything except that he mounts it, because he does not believe in Allah, does not forbid what He has forbidden, and does not make lawful what He has made lawful; rather, his religion is only what his own self desires, and he acts upon it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god﴾, he said: That is the disbeliever who has taken his religion without guidance from Allah or any proof.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god﴾, he said: He does not desire anything except that he mounts it, not fearing Allah.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Have you seen him who has taken as his object of worship whatever his own self desires to worship, of any thing.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: Quraysh used to worship al-'Uzza, which was a white stone, for a period of time; then, when they found something better than it, they cast off the first and worshipped the other. So Allah revealed ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god﴾.

The more correct of the two interpretations in this matter is the view of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Have you seen, O Muhammad, him who has taken as his object of worship his desire, so that he worships whatever thing he desires, apart from the God of truth to whom divinity belongs over everything, because that is the apparent meaning of it rather than any other.

* *

As for His words ﴿and Allah has misguided him knowingly﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He forsook him from the clear path and the way of right guidance in His prior knowledge, knowing that he will not be guided, even if every sign came to him.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning that.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and Allah has misguided him knowingly﴾, he said: Allah misguided him in His prior knowledge.

* *

As for His words ﴿and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He sealed his hearing so that he does not hear the admonitions of Allah and the verses of His Book, so that he would take heed from them, reflect upon them, and ponder them, and thereby understand what is in them of light, clarity and guidance.

* *

As for His words ﴿and his heart﴾:

He says: He also sealed his heart, so that he understands nothing with it and comprehends no truth through it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and has put a covering upon his sight﴾:

He says: He placed a covering upon his sight, so that he does not see with it the proofs of Allah, by which he would reason to His oneness and know through them that there is no god but Him.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿and has put a covering upon his sight﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some readers of Kufa recited ﴿ghishawah﴾ with a kasrah on the ghayn and an alif affirmed in it, as a noun. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿ghashwah﴾ with a fatha on the ghayn and without an alif, meaning that He covered it with something in a single act, one time. Both of these, in my view, are correct recitations, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct.

* *

As for His words ﴿Who then will guide him after Allah﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Who will grant him success in reaching the truth and seeing the path of right guidance after Allah has misguided him? ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ O people, so that you may know that whoever Allah has done to him what we have described, he will never be guided, and will never find for himself a guiding protector.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 24:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And they say: There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us but time. And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾

His, the Exalted's, remembrance says: These polytheists, whose report He has previously mentioned, said: "There is no life but our life of this world in which we are, no other life," denying resurrection after death.

As follows:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And they say: There is nothing but our life of this world﴾: meaning, "By my life, this is the saying of the polytheists of the Arabs."

* *

As for His words ﴿we die and we live﴾:

We die, and we live, and our children live after us. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾: "This is the Day of Resurrection, kneeling upon their knees."

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾: "Upon their knees at the reckoning."

* *

As for His words ﴿Every nation will be called to its record﴾:

He says: every people of a religion and creed will be called to their record which was dictated to their recording angels.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Every nation will be called to its record﴾: "They know that one nation will be called before another nation, and one people before another people, and one man before another man." It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "On the Day of Resurrection there will be presented to every nation what it used to worship, whether a stone, an idol, a piece of wood, or an animal. He said: 'Do you suffer any harm from the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no cloud over it?' They said: No, O Messenger of Allah. He said: 'Indeed you will see Him on the Day of Resurrection in the same way. Allah will gather the people and say: Whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will be the first to cross it, and the supplication of the messengers on that day will be: O Allah, grant safety, O Allah, grant safety. He said: "They are like the thorns of the sa'dan, except that none knows their magnitude except Allah. His saying, may He be remembered, means: As for those who believed in God in this world, so that they affirmed His oneness and did not associate anything with Him, and did righteous deeds, meaning: they acted upon what God commanded them and refrained from what God forbade them, ﴿their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾, meaning into His Garden by His mercy.

* *

As for His saying ﴿That is the clear triumph﴾:

He says: Their entry into the mercy of God on that day is the attainment of what they used to seek and the reaching of what they used to strive for in the world. The clear (al-mubin) aspect of their goal in it is that this is the triumph.

**The discourse on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, [it will be said:] "Were not My verses recited to you? But you were arrogant, and you were a criminal people."﴾ (45:31)**

His, exalted is He, saying: "As for those who denied the oneness of God and refused to single Him out in worship during the world, it will be said to them: Were not My verses recited to you in the world?"

If someone says: "Is not *ammā* (as for) answered by a *fā'* (then)? Where is it?" The answer is that it is the *fā'* in His saying ﴿then has not﴾ (*afa-lam*). The original structure of the sentence in Arabic, if it were pronounced in its full form, and its underlying form, would be: "As for those who disbelieved, then were not My verses recited to you?" This is because the meaning of the sentence is: "As for those who disbelieved, it will be said to them: Has not..." So the position of the *fā'* is at the beginning of the omitted element, which is required by the sense of the sentence. When that element is omitted, the interrogative *alif* (the hamzah of interrogation) comes, and its rule is that it must be placed at the beginning, so it is placed first and the *fā'* is placed after it.

The Arabs sometimes drop the *fā'* that answers *ammā* in such a position, when they omit the verb that stands in the place of the answer to *ammā*, as in His, may He be praised, saying: ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾. The *fā'* was dropped because the verb that stands as the answer to *ammā*, namely *fa-yuqālu* (it will be said), was omitted. The meaning of the sentence is: "As for those whose faces turned black, it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve?" So when the verb was dropped, the *fā'* that connects the answer was dropped along with it, and the *fā'* that answers *ammā* was dropped.

* *

As for His saying ﴿but you were arrogant﴾:

He says: you were arrogant about listening to them and believing in them. ﴿And you were a criminal people﴾: He says: you were a people who earned sins and disbelief in God, and you did not affirm a return (to God), nor did you believe in reward or punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 32:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour - there is no doubt about it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is. We only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: and it will be said to them at that time: ﴿And when it was said to you, "Indeed, the promise of Allah"﴾ which He promised His servants, that He will bring them back to life after their death and raise them from their graves, ﴿is true, and the Hour﴾ which He informed them that He will establish for the gathering of them and the assembling of them for reckoning and reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience, is coming ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾. He means: there is no doubt about it, meaning the Hour. The pronoun in His words ﴿about it﴾ refers to the Hour. The meaning of the statement is: the Hour, there is no doubt about its establishment, so fear Allah, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and work for what will save you from the punishment of Allah in it. ﴿You said, "We do not know what the Hour is"﴾ as a denial on your part of the promise of Allah, may His majesty be praised, a rejection of His report, and a denial of His power to bring you back to life after your death.

* *

As for His words ﴿We only assume an assumption﴾:

He says: and you said, "We only assume that the Hour is coming, an assumption," ﴿and we are not certain﴾ that it is coming, nor that it will occur.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿and the Hour, there is no doubt about it﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the readers of Kufa, recited it ﴿the Hour﴾ in the nominative as an inceptive (mubtada'). And the majority of the readers of Kufa recited it "wa-as-sa'ata" in the accusative, conjoining it to His words ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾.

The correct view on this matter in our opinion is that they are two widely transmitted recitations in the recitation of the regions, both sound in their linguistic basis (i'rab) and close in meaning, so whichever of the two the reciter reads is correct.

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And there will appear to them the evil of what they did, and there will befall them that which they used to mock﴾ (45:33).

He, exalted is His mention, says: And there will appear to those who used to disbelieve in the signs of God in the world the evils of what they did in the world of deeds, meaning: there will become apparent to them then their ugliness and their wickedness when they read their books of deeds, which the guardian angels had been recording in the world. ﴿And there will befall them that which they used to mock﴾ means: there will befall them then, of the punishment of God, that which they used to mock, when it was said to them: indeed God will make it descend upon whoever denied it, for the evil deeds of what they did in the world.

* *

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day; and your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers"﴾ (45:34).

He, exalted is His mention, says: And it will be said to these disbelievers whose description has been given: Today We will leave you in the punishment of the Hellfire, just as you left off works for the meeting of your Lord on this your Day.

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you"﴾: "We will leave you."

* *

It means: your abode to which you retreat is the Fire of Hell. ﴿And you have no helpers﴾ means: and you have no rescuer who will save you today from the punishment of God, nor any defender who will defend you against the one who punishes you, so as to rescue you from him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 45, verses 35–37:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you.﴾ So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be asked to make amends.

Exalted is He, He says: It will be said to them: This which has befallen you today of the punishment of Allah is ﴿because you﴾ in the world ﴿took the signs of Allah in mockery﴾, and they are His proofs, His arguments, and the verses of His Book which He sent down to His Messenger ﷺ, ﴿in mockery﴾, meaning you mocked them. ﴿And the worldly life deceived you﴾ means: the adornment of the worldly life deceived you. So you preferred it over acting for that which would save you today from the punishment of Allah. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it﴾ from the Fire, ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. It means: nor will they be returned to the world to repent and turn back in penitence from that for which they were punished.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of all the worlds. And to Him belongs grandeur throughout the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.﴾

Exalted is He, He says: ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise﴾ for His blessings and favours upon His creation. So it is to Him alone that you should give praise, O people, for every blessing you have is from Him, not from what you worship besides Him of gods and idols, nor from what you take besides Him as lords and associate with Him. ﴿Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth﴾: He says, the Owner of the seven heavens and the Owner of the seven earths. And ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾: He says, the Owner of all that is in them of kinds of creation. And ﴿to Him belongs grandeur throughout the heavens and the earth﴾: He says, to Him belongs majesty and dominion throughout the heavens and the earth, not what is other than Him of gods and rivals. ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ in His vengeance upon His enemies, subduing everything beneath Him, and nothing overpowers Him. ﴿The Wise﴾ in His management of His creation and His disposing of them in what He wills, however He wills. And Allah knows best.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Jathiyah.
